description:
Read only the profiler report from the previous task and produce an executable NAS search space plan in JSON.
Behavior requirements: - Be conservative and pragmatic. - Prefer simple, well-established model families. - Include only model families clearly supported by profiler evidence. - Use small, bounded, realistic hyperparameter ranges. - Prefer categorical choices and small discrete ranges over wide continuous spaces. - Express uncertainty when profiler evidence is incomplete.
Strict constraints: - Do not inspect raw datasets. - Do not call dataset inspection tools. - Do not train models. - Do not run Optuna. - Do not evaluate model performance. - Do not select a final model.
Output must be strict JSON only (no markdown, no code fences, no prose before/after JSON).
\n\nInput: use only the profiler report generated by the previous task.

key_constraints: Input dimensionality is high (2500 features) relative to sample size (2660 samples)
Fixed sequence length of 2500 requires architectures capable of handling long-range dependencies
Small sample size necessitates high regularization to prevent overfitting

selected_model_families.rationale: The 2500 sequential features indicate 1D signal data. 1D Convolutions are well-suited for extracting local morphological features from ECG signals while remaining more parameter-efficient than RNNs or large MLPs.
Standard baseline for numeric vectors. Included as a low-complexity alternative, though it ignores the sequential nature of the data.

uncertainty_notes: Sampling rate is unknown, so 'kernel_size' ranges are speculative and cover both narrow and wide receptive fields.
The 2500 points may represent a single heartbeat or multiple cycles; the appropriate level of downsampling/pooling is uncertain.
handoff_notes: Deduplicate the 56 identified rows before starting the search to avoid evaluation bias.
Focus on cnn1d as the primary candidate; keep model depth low (max 4 layers) to avoid overfitting the 2.6k samples.
Since classes are balanced, Accuracy or F1-score are suitable optimization metrics.
